title: House Robber IV
summary: Given an integer array nums where nums[i] represents the amount of money in the i-th house, and an integer k indicating the minimum number of houses the robber must rob, determine the minimum capability the robber can have.
statement: Given an integer array nums where nums[i] represents the amount of money in the i-th house, and an integer k indicating the minimum number of houses the robber must rob, determine the minimum capability the robber can have. The robber's capability is defined as the maximum amount of money stolen from any single house among the houses robbed. The robber cannot rob two adjacent houses.
constraints: Rob at least k houses without choosing adjacent indices.
Capability is the largest value among robbed houses.
hints: For a fixed threshold, greedily rob the earliest eligible house and skip its neighbor.
Count whether this scan reaches at least k houses.
Feasibility is monotone, and choosing an earlier eligible house leaves at least as much room as any later choice, validating both greedy checking and binary search.
editorial: Feasibility is monotone, and choosing an earlier eligible house leaves at least as much room as any later choice, validating both greedy checking and binary search.

tests.explanation: Houses zero and two are nonadjacent and cap the maximum robbed value at five.
Robbing values two and one yields the minimum capability two.
